blocks.content: Introduction to FOD and tool accountability
Take correct actions to prevent FOD; do not close up until hardware is accounted for.

items.definition: The most effective FOD prevention practice is strict tool control: count tools BEFORE and AFTER every job, and immediately retrieve and clean up any dropped hardware or debris.
items.analogy: Like a surgeon counting instruments before and after an operation — every item must be accounted for, because a missing one means something dangerous was left inside.

items.definition: If a screw is dropped behind a panel during avionics installation: (1) STOP work, (2) retrieve the screw BEFORE closing any panels, (3) log it as a FOD prevention measure.
items.analogy: Like a surgeon who drops an instrument inside a patient — you stop the procedure, retrieve the item, and document it. You don't close up and hope for the best.

blocks.question: Which practice is MOST effective at preventing Foreign Object Damage (FOD) in an avionics shop?
choices: Using only snap-on toolboxes with latching lids
Strict tool control — counting tools before and after each job and immediately cleaning up dropped hardware
Performing tool inventory once per week
Restricting shop access to credentialed technicians only
blocks.feedback: Tool control is the foundation of FOD prevention — counting tools before and after every job ensures nothing is left inside an aircraft, and immediate cleanup of dropped hardware prevents items from migrating into aircraft structure.

blocks.question: During avionics installation, a screw drops behind a panel and is not immediately visible. What is the correct action?
choices: Close the panel and notify QC on the job card
Complete the installation and perform a final FOD walk after
Replace the missing screw with a spare and note the discrepancy on the work order
Stop work, retrieve the screw before closing any panels, and log the event
blocks.feedback: No panel may be closed until the dropped hardware is retrieved. A missing screw inside an aircraft structure is a serious FOD hazard, and the event must be logged per FOD prevention procedures.
